item.title: Arctic power plays: EU searches for a new strategy
item.description: Russia’s aggression, Trump’s threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe’s agenda.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
item.description: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
item.description: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: IPO 'for the people' is out of reach for many in Nigeria
item.description: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Nepal: thousands still missing as flood recovery begins
item.description: The Himalayan nation is moving from rescue operations to recovery, facing a $4.8 billion reconstruction bill amid renewed calls for climate justice.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
item.description: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Pay to ghost your boss: Japan's resignation business
item.description: Resignation agencies in Japan help employees leave their jobs seamlessly in just 15 minutes. Young people are especially eager to use their services.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Israeli minister accuses 'NAZA' filmmakers of 'treason'
item.description: Israel's culture minister wants to strip the makers of a documentary on Israel's Gaza offensive of their citizenship. He accused the two of seeking "applause from antisemites around the world."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
item.description: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.
item.dc:subject: Business

item.title: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
item.description: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
item.description: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump visits Ireland, says unification would be 'fantastic'
item.description: US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Uganda lays 'boy king' Oyo to rest amid succession row
item.description: Uganda has buried King Oyo Nyimba, who was crowned in the Tooro Kingdom in 1995 aged just 3. His death at 34 has triggered a dispute over a successor, as rumors abound of possible heirs born out of wedlock.
